evidence: src/infrastructure/http/createApp.ts: createApp({ orders, stock }: Controllers) only registers routes that point to controller methods (stock.list, orders.place, orders.pay, ...) and then adds notFoundHandler and errorHandler.

src/infrastructure/http/requestParsing.ts: the doc comment on parsePlaceOrderBody says 'Checks the shape of an untrusted request body; business rules are enforced by the domain', so the work is split cleanly with the domain.
src/infrastructure/http/requestParsing.ts: parseStateQuery calls the domain's isOrderStatus instead of copying the list of valid order statuses, so that rule stays in one place.
src/infrastructure/http/requestParsing.ts: parseLine and parsePlaceOrderBody check only types (string or number, array) and leave quantity and other business checks to the domain.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files belong to the same concern: the HTTP adapter at the edge of the infrastructure layer. createApp.ts builds the Express app and registers routes and middleware. requestParsing.ts turns untrusted request input into application DTOs. No rule is duplicated. The parser only checks the shape of the input, as its doc comment says, and leaves business rules to the domain. It reuses the domain's isOrderStatus check instead of copying the list of valid statuses, and it throws the domain's ValidationError. createApp sends all request handling through the injected controllers and shared middleware instead of handling requests inline. The only exception is a trivial /health endpoint, which doesn't skip any of the module's own abstractions.
